title: A federal IT services RFP with 47 illustrative requirements
description: This fictional federal IT services scenario combines service delivery, staffing, past performance, and a structured price submission. The illustrative workload spans both scope and response instructions.

The example assumes a 30-day response window and an estimated value in the $500K to $5M band. Its counts are authored to demonstrate a review approach; they are not results from a real solicitation or an actual shredder run.

dealBreakers: A required past-performance format can make an otherwise relevant example unusable. In this fictional scenario, the bidder must verify the requested fields and structure before drafting.
A pricing-table rule appears in an attachment reference. The bidder must obtain and review that attachment rather than assume the main narrative is the complete instruction set.
lesson: The mandatory count, not the page count, sets the workload. Count obligations across scope, submission instructions, and referenced attachments before allocating bid hours.

faq.question: Where do teardowns come from?
faq.answer: These launch teardowns are authored fictional examples based on common solicitation shapes. Their counts are illustrative, not measured results from real bids or visitor submissions.

faq.question: Can I get my solicitation torn down?
faq.answer: Use the free shredder or bid checker privately. A public teardown requires separate human review, anonymization, and your explicit confirmation. Publication is never automatic.

faq.question: Does a teardown guarantee anything?
faq.answer: No. A teardown does not certify compliance or predict an award. Verify the original solicitation, attachments, and amendments before making a bid decision.
